# Estuary Restoration Compendium

This compendium gathers field notes and design guidance from a coastal wetland
restoration programme. The material is organised into numbered parts, each
describing one aspect of the work in plain technical prose.

## Part 1: Tidal Reconnection

Reconnecting drained land to the tide restores the daily cycle of inundation that
a marsh depends on.

### 1.1 Background

Before any breach is cut, the elevation of the site is surveyed against the tidal
frame so that the depth and frequency of flooding can be predicted.

### 1.2 Practice

The breach is sized to the tidal prism, the volume of water exchanged on each
tide; too small and the site stagnates, too large and the velocities scour the bank.
